title: IntentDecision
description: What the sender of one message wants, plus the meeting time extracted from it when there is one. Separate from AIDecision, which answers whether to interrupt the user rather than what to do about the message.

messageId.description: Must exactly match the classified ExternalMessage.id. Inject it from the request rather than having the model reproduce it: asked to echo an identifier such as 'slack:C08ABCDEF:1789788720.000200', a small model drops a digit.

intent.description: meeting_invite: the sender is stating a specific meeting time that is already decided. other: anything else, including a message that merely asks to find a time. When unsure, other.

confidence.description: How sure the classification is, from 0 to 1. The consumer sets its own threshold; acting on a calendar is harder to undo than showing a notification, so a higher bar is reasonable here than elsewhere.

reason.description: Short human-readable explanation, never a command to execute.

startTime.description: Extracted meeting start, with an explicit offset. Null, and only null, when no usable time could be read out of the message. Present only for intent meeting_invite.

endTime.description: Exclusive end, later than startTime; that relationship is checked by the consumer. Given in the same shape as ExternalEvent and the calendar API so the value passes straight through without unit arithmetic. When the message states no duration the engine applies its own default and says so in reason.

title.description: Suggested calendar title, in the language of the message. Null when none could be derived.
